title: MESH render tree, version 1
description: What the MESH runtime's render produces and a renderer draws (see docs/manual/runtime.md): primitive components, their prop values, text, event names with handler identifiers, and keys. Nothing else: no expression, scope name, command, argument, composite, template, span or $event. Values are final, so a renderer computes nothing. This schema lists exactly the properties this MESH produces. A later MESH may add properties without changing `version`; removing one or changing its meaning is a new version. Renderers must ignore properties they don't know. `$defs/intent` is the command intent dispatch produces for a host, under the same promise; a renderer never sees one.

root.description: The root node: the root template's root element, or, if that is a composite occurrence, what its template produced.

key.description: A node's or text run's structural identity: unique in the tree, the same at the same position in every render of the program, and independent of values. Opaque: compare keys for equality, and never interpret them.

handler.description: An opaque handler identifier. A renderer reports it, with the event's payload, when the event fires, and never interprets it.

value.description: A value from the boundary data model (§9.8): null, a boolean, a finite number (never -0), a string, a list of values, or a record of values. An absent value is never here: an absent prop or record field is simply missing.

props.description: Each written prop's value, by prop name. An absent prop has no member here; a `null` prop is `null`.

events.description: For each event binding, its event name and handler identifier.

children.description: Nodes and text runs, in order.

text.description: A text run: the text of a maximal sequence of adjacent literal text and interpolations. Present even when empty.

intent.description: A command intent: which command a handler invoked, and its evaluated arguments. Dispatch gives it to the host, never to a renderer.

command.description: The command's identity: its name, and the component whose template declares it.

arguments.description: One entry per parameter, in parameter order.

oneOf.description: An absent argument, where the parameter's type is optional. Distinct from `{ "value": null }`.
